site.name: Will AI Replace Me?
site.tagline: A calm, launch-ready homepage for the future AI role assessment journey.

hero.title: Will AI Replace Me?
hero.description: This first release focuses on a trustworthy narrative, a clear methodology frame, and stable UI foundations before real assessment logic arrives.

stats.title: Static landing first
stats.description: The launch version delivers the homepage architecture, hero, explainer blocks, and future entry points without pretending unfinished interactions are ready.

stats.title: Full UI baseline
stats.description: The site already carries builder-style shadcn primitives, Tailwind tokens, and responsive layout conventions.

stats.title: Ready for complex forms
stats.description: Future questionnaires, steps, and result cards can plug into the same control system, spacing rhythm, and interaction language.

story.sectionTitle: Translate “Will AI replace me?” into a clearer personal audit
story.sectionDescription: The launch version does not pretend to answer everything. It turns the question into a structure people can understand and future releases can extend.

cards.title: Start with the question people already ask
cards.description: The homepage leads with the simplest question so new visitors immediately understand the purpose and scope of the site.

cards.title: Build the reliable shell before business logic
cards.description: The first release prioritizes build tooling, language, SEO, theming, and components so later iterations can move faster.

cards.title: Say clearly what is not implemented yet
cards.description: The site makes future slots explicit instead of pretending that unfinished assessment features already exist.

methodology.title: Methodology first: the future result should be more than yes or no
methodology.description: The real assessment will eventually connect task breakdowns, automation signals, human strengths, and next-step recommendations. For now, the structure and tone are in place.

pillars.title: Task-level analysis
pillars.description: The future flow should analyze work tasks rather than job titles alone to produce more credible explanations.

pillars.title: Industry context
pillars.description: The same role behaves differently across industries and organizations, so context needs a place in the future form flow.

pillars.title: Human advantage
pillars.description: The result should explain not only what can be automated, but also the human strengths that remain valuable.

methodology.note: For now, this section is intentionally a summary placeholder so the next change can expand it without rebuilding the shell.
nextItems: • A shared visual baseline for future shadcn form journeys

formBlueprint.title: A static blueprint for the future complex form experience
formBlueprint.description: This is where role inputs, task mapping, progressive steps, and result generation will connect later. For now it validates layout density, disabled states, accessibility, and component styling.

labels.context: What work do you most want to examine?

placeholders.role: For example: product marketer, solutions engineer, backend developer
placeholders.industry: For example: education, manufacturing, consumer brand
placeholders.context: For example: I handle customer conversations, workflow coordination, and editorial packaging. Which parts are easier to automate?

formBlueprint.helper: These fields will connect to real validation and multi-step assessment flows in a future change. Today they exist as structure and styling slots.
formBlueprint.contractDescription: This slot is reserved for the real multi-step form flow, field validation, result summaries, and recommendation actions.
formBlueprint.contractNote: The current release calibrates layout density, form styling, disabled states, focus rings, and content containers so the next change can plug real logic straight in.

futureFeatures.sectionTitle: Future capabilities should not pretend to be live in v1
futureFeatures.sectionDescription: The homepage exposes clear entry points, structural placeholders, and honest status labels. The real question bank, scoring, and result explanations will grow from these cards later.

jobProfile.title: Role profile intake
jobProfile.description: Collect the role, industry, target tasks, and surrounding context before scoring begins.

taskBreakdown.title: Task breakdown prompts
taskBreakdown.description: Add realistic questions that capture the difference between a job title and the actual work inside it.

resultBrief.title: Risk result brief
resultBrief.description: Summarize replacement risk, automatable work, human advantage, and clear interpretation instead of a raw score only.

actionPath.title: Action recommendation cards
actionPath.description: Translate the future risk profile into concrete next steps for skills, tooling, or role redesign.

footer.disclaimer: This page is currently a demonstration of information architecture and interaction foundations. It is not career, legal, or financial advice, and future results should remain decision support rather than absolute truth.
footer.extensionNote: Static assets, SEO metadata, theme tokens, and shadcn control foundations are already wired in so future product work can stay focused on real behavior.
